newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 16.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* Consumer prices rose one-tenth of 1 percent in April.
* Hewlett-Packard Co's Q2 earnings were up but fell short of analysts' expectations.
* Swiss Bank Corp has agreed to acquire Wall Street investment bank Dillon, Read & Co for $600 million.
* Airbus Industrie has signed a $1.5 billion deal to supply jets to China.
* Kmart Corp posted a profit in its first quarter for the first time since 1994, while Saks Holdings Inc and Gap Inc reported strong results as well.
* The National Association of Securities Dealers fined a New York brokerage and its former principal more than $5 million, contending it had manipulated the stock of a bedding company.
* Time Warner Inc is being criticized by the chairwoman of the National Political Congress of Black Women for sexually explicit lyrics of one of its rap artists.
* The dollar fell against the Japanese yen close to the same level where it started the year.
* The planned sale of the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team to News Corp Ltd's Fox network reflects a new era in sports ownership.
* Price Waterhouse LLT has agreed to consolidate in New York City, adding more than 1,000 workers, and will receive $2 million in state grants.
* United Breweries Group, India's largest beer maker and distributor, plans to buy small U.S. brewers.
* Two New Jersey investors have been charged with perjury in a federal investigation into possible insider trading in shares of Lotus Development Corp before it was acquired by IBM in 1995.

* United Airlines plans to begin airing a new ad campaign on Thursday that contrasts sharply with most airline advertisements. Rather than peddling "friendly skies," United is planning a campaign that empathizes with some of the hassles.
* Since a venture between Ford Motor Co and Volkswagen AG to manufacture cars in Brazil and Argentina failed, VW's fortunes have risen in the region while Ford's have stumbled.
* A judge has ruled that Viacom Inc violated a partnership with Seagram Co Ltd.
